stem: A KPI moves in the same direction for four cycles, but each cycle used a different time window. What is the main problem?
choices: Treat four same-direction values as a valid trend because consistency across four cycles outweighs time-window differences.
Standardize or otherwise reconcile the time-window definition before interpreting the four values as directly comparable trend evidence.
Ignore time-window differences if the numerator and denominator definitions stayed the same.
Remove the lowest value and interpret the remaining three because different windows mainly affect extremes.
rationale: A KPI measured over different time windows may represent different exposure, opportunity, or workload even when the formula is otherwise unchanged. Same-direction movement across incomparable windows can be suggestive, but it is not a clean trend until the observation window is standardized or the difference is explicitly accounted for.
